items.title: Reject unsupported production receipt algorithms fail-closed
items.context: Determine whether production receipt verification currently accepts serverKey.algorithm values other than ed25519. If it does, add the smallest runtime guard and focused smoke coverage so unsupported signature/public-key algorithms never satisfy production receipt verification.
items.userSees: User sees authority receipt verification reject unsupported algorithms with an explicit fail-closed reason, while ed25519 receipt tests still pass.

happy.desc: Verify a production receipt whose serverKey.algorithm is ed25519 and whose signature/public key are otherwise valid -> verification succeeds exactly as before; WHY: proves the new guard does not regress the supported algorithm path.

edge.desc: Verify a production receipt whose serverKey.algorithm is missing or uses case/format variants such as ED25519 or ed-25519 -> verification fails closed with an explicit unsupported-algorithm reason instead of silently normalizing; WHY: enforces a single consistent algorithm contract.

adversarial.desc: Verify a production receipt whose signature payload is otherwise valid but serverKey.algorithm is an unsupported value such as rsa or secp256k1 -> verification must reject before any success path and must not accept the receipt due to incidental crypto compatibility; WHY: prevents arbitrary algorithm expansion and proves fail-closed correctness.

items.title: Converge supportsDryRun requirement without speculative metadata work
items.context: Inspect the old cc-learnings ToolDef metadata requirement against current COMMAND_POLICIES, command schemas, and dryRun handlers. Either implement a real supportsDryRun metadata surface consumed by help/policy, or narrow the truth source to the current command-policy contract if the old ToolDef field was superseded.
items.userSees: User sees gap_analyze no longer report supportsDryRun?: boolean, with dry-run semantics documented or implemented in the single current command contract.

happy.desc: Run the user-facing command/help/policy surface after the contract change -> gap_analyze and command metadata expose exactly one current dry-run contract and no longer require a stale supportsDryRun field; WHY: proves the truth source was converged rather than papered over.

edge.desc: Exercise a command that supports dry-run and a command that does not -> the reported/help-visible policy must match actual handler behavior for both, without inventing metadata for commands that lack real dry-run semantics; WHY: catches inconsistent logic between docs/policy and runtime.

adversarial.desc: Attempt to satisfy the gap by adding speculative supportsDryRun-style metadata that is not consumed by the live command-policy/help path -> verification should fail unless the surfaced contract is mechanically tied to current runtime behavior; WHY: blocks arbitrary optimization and metadata-only fixes.

items.title: Link Authority worktree policy requirements to existing runtime enforcement
items.context: For requiresAuthoritativeWorktree and requiresCleanWorktree, verify existing planner emission, consistency checks, executor preflight, dirty worktree handling, and smoke tests. Add precise code annotations or minimal tests only where the gap is coverage linkage, not behavior.
items.userSees: User sees gap_analyze no longer report requiresAuthoritativeWorktree or requiresCleanWorktree, and worktree-policy smoke tests still prove fail-closed enforcement.

happy.desc: Run the existing authoritative-worktree/clean-worktree smoke path in the expected authoritative worktree state -> planner emission, executor preflight, and smoke evidence all agree that the command proceeds when policy requirements are satisfied; WHY: proves the documented requirement is already enforced by runtime logic.

edge.desc: Run the same flow in a clean but non-authoritative worktree, and separately in an authoritative but dirty worktree -> each requirement fails for its own specific reason without conflating the two policies; WHY: proves consistency of the two gates and their diagnostics.

adversarial.desc: Try to clear the gap only by adding requirement prose or planner annotations while leaving any enforcement path unproven by smoke coverage -> verification should fail unless runtime evidence still demonstrates fail-closed blocking for both requiresAuthoritativeWorktree and requiresCleanWorktree; WHY: disallows coverage-link claims that are host- or reviewer-opinion-only.

items.title: Link planner confirmation policy to story creation blocking behavior
items.context: For requiresConfirmationBeforeStoryCreate, verify default plannerPolicy behavior and planner_create_story blocking behavior. Add precise coverage linkage or focused regression only if current tests do not prove fail-closed story creation.
items.userSees: User sees gap_analyze no longer report requiresConfirmationBeforeStoryCreate, and planner tests prove story creation blocks until confirmation when policy requires it.

happy.desc: Run planner story-creation flow when plannerPolicy requires confirmation and explicit confirmation is present -> story creation proceeds and the policy/result surface shows the confirmation gate was satisfied; WHY: proves the intended unblock path still works.

edge.desc: Run the same flow under a policy/profile that does not require confirmation -> story creation behavior matches that policy without inheriting the stricter gate accidentally; WHY: verifies the requirement is policy-driven rather than globally hardcoded.

adversarial.desc: Attempt planner_create_story without the required confirmation while all other inputs are valid -> it must fail closed before creating the story and must not rely on downstream cleanup to undo partial creation; WHY: proves real blocking behavior instead of post-hoc remediation.

items.title: Prove gap convergence and host-neutral review evidence
items.context: Run gap_analyze before/after, relevant focused tests, and lattice validate. Record Codex host execution evidence and two Claude CLI host review attempts or availability downgrades as advisory evidence, while keeping Lattice CLI/test outputs as the authoritative gate facts.
items.userSees: User sees lattice gap_analyze report Gaps: 0 high / 0 medium and the story summary explains that host reviews are advisory while Lattice tests/evidence are authoritative.
